signals.title: NZD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags CHF as the weekly outperformer at +0.683% across 6 pairs while NZD acts as the primary laggard at −0.417% across 4 pairs, creating a 1.100% spread. NZD/USD trades at 0.5472, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 0.5567) in a clear downtrend. The economic surprise index underscores this divergence, with CHF registering a strong positive +28.0 ESI versus NZD running a strong negative −15.4 ESI. RBNZ at 2.75% versus SNB at 0.00% maintains a 275bp nominal carry advantage for NZD, but market pricing and macro data momentum favor CHF outperformance. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/CHF, broad G10 divergence setup. Catalyst: RBNZ Board Member speech and upcoming New Zealand data releases. Risk: Global risk sentiment rebounds sharply, compressing the 1.100% G10 spread below the 0.80% threshold.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Volatility Risk Premium + Positioning Extreme
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.15, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster with the SMA20 at 158.69. A 275bp Fed-BoJ rate differential (SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23% for +269bp OIS carry) maintains fundamental support for the pair. However, options market pricing reveals significant protection demand, with 1M ATM IV at 7.7% against HV30 at 5.5% (a 2.2% vol risk premium) and 25d risk reversals showing a steep put skew of −1.87. CFTC Leveraged Funds net short JPY sits at −29,545 contracts (85th percentile of its 52-week range), leaving positioning crowded near resistance. 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered verbal warnings, and intervention risk rises on a sustained break above 160.00. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-driven while VIX stays contained. Catalyst: BoJ Trimmed Mean Core CPI release. Risk: VIX breaks above 25.0 alongside sharp downside options unwinds, triggering a disorderly carry liquidation.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CB Hawkish Stance vs Positioning Unwind
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3093, remaining below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.3289, SMA50 at 1.3293). BoE’s Greene reiterated hawkish guidance in fresh comments, stating monetary policy must anchor inflation expectations and that a turnaround in data or war is needed to change views. BoE policy rate at 4.00% vs Fed 4.00% (SONIA 3.98% vs SOFR 3.92%) provides a neutral carry backdrop. CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net long GBP at +23,730 contracts (38th percentile), but a WoW reduction of −11,856 contracts indicates institutional longs are trimming into rallies. BEER model misvaluation shows GBP/USD cheap at z=-1.83σ relative to fair value of 1.3170. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD on hawkish BoE policy support. Catalyst: US Core PCE Price Index release. Risk: A downside break in UK CBI data follow-through that forces money markets to reprice BoE rate path expectations.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Sentiment Divergence + Policy Outlook
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4331, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.4158). Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.50% delivers a +150bp nominal policy differential (+136bp OIS carry advantage for USD), maintaining underlying structural support. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows extreme crowding with 92% of retail accounts short USD/CAD (8% long), creating a sharp divergence against CFTC Leveraged Funds who hold a net short CAD position of −75,447 contracts (22.5% long). BEER model metrics rank USD/CAD rich at z=+2.31σ above model fair value of 1.4245, suggesting upside extension faces valuation friction. Governor Tiff Macklem's upcoming speech at the Economic Club of Canada serves as the immediate policy driver. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD, supported by retail contrarian setup and carry differential. Catalyst: BoC Governor Macklem speech. Risk: Tiff Macklem delivers unexpectedly hawkish guidance that compresses the 150bp policy rate spread.
